 December
editions.body_excerpt:
View this post on the web at https://www.latent.space/p/ainews-glm-gpt-glm-52-passes-vibe

Don’t miss out on our Anj Midha episode [ https://substack.com/redirect/dc71209b-b62a-49b5-8a7c-61b679292831?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] today and regular tix for AIE World’s Fair [ https://substack.com/redirect/8a3912cd-cb51-4e89-8d45-2fd5bf84b772?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]!
In the AI News business, there’s a bit of trepidation talking about open models: they come out guns blazing, looking pretty on notable benchmarks, and then a month later they fade into disuse like they never existed. In other words: they were “benchmaxxed”. And we hate reporting news that you won’t remember here at LS.
One of the policies readers tell us they like about AINews is that we will simply say if nothing much happened today [ https://substack.com/redirect/84a36fd5-3ffe-4902-af09-558663a01ba9?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] (a newsletter that tells you that you can skip it is rare, partly because we don’t have an eyeballs driven business model.). Increasingly, we’ve also tried to do the inverse — repeatedly [ https://substack.com/redirect/72b57bc5-14eb-4b15-afc3-21eda5c3806c?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] calling [ https://substack.com/redirect/35e81d49-68b9-48ba-8c37-3bc8491ff45a?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]out [ https://substack.com/redirect/d0df1013-548b-4b84-940b-7af83a609e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] a notable trend is just as important as filtering out low signal.
GLM 5 passed that bar, and GLM 5.1 didn’t. GLM 5.2 [ https://substack.com/redirect/6e9f1d31-8934-4933-abd7-69ba8f889593?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], which we reported on 2 days ago, felt a little different, and that instinct was confirmed today, with multiple out of sample datapoints passing the “this is a frontier model that just happens to be open” vibe check:
Jeremy Howard, friend of the show [ https://substack.com/redirect/35894794-8976-4910-a120-990dadfe8158?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] not given to hype, sincerely complimenting [ https://substack.com/redirect/b1376fc8-b8af-4dc9-b387-a800fcdf7e8b?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] it:
and Artificial Analysis’ new knowledge work benchmark [ https://substack.com/redirect/3ee07430-a6e5-46dc-b479-74e6a0a8cdf3?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] rates it higher than GPT 5.5:
And it is passing the /r/LocalLlama vibe check [ https://substack.com/redirect/180e5382-a9f4-4df8-be73-30f942294f5b?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]:
This trajectory of Z.ai getting validation as a true frontier lab is now a serious trend; the final milestone of (Chinese) open models winning is the timeline for when we will get an open Fable-class model, without the possibility of distillation attacks (Z.ai was notably missing from the list of accused Chinese labs in Anthropic’s Feb “industrial-scale distillation” report [ https://substack.com/redirect/0d6fca21-69a0-4b49-9cc3-7f61ea2c57cf?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]):
The tricky question no one can answer is - will any of the top 4 labs be able to release another Fable-class model again in the next 6 months, or has the ongoing Mythos ban [ https://substack.com/redirect/3b83464a-1a3c-4ca5-8bb7-17e37f7a5749?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] put everything on ice?
AI News for 6/17/2026-6/18/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters [ https://substack.com/redirect/500d29ac-0d5e-41e1-898f-932a1b5a2716?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] and no further Discords. AINews’ website [ https://substack.com/redirect/0fb34901-2a6c-45b0-a48a-cd598631edc6?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space [ https://substack.com/redirect/8c180aef-c3a7-4558-aec6-5dd59e00a0ed?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]. You can opt in/out [ https://substack.com/redirect/9f689a03-d6c8-4b5f-9b47-9d1efa0d8422?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] of email frequencies!
AI Twitter Recap
GLM-5.2’s Breakout, Open-Weight Coding Progress, and New Open Models
GLM-5.2 became the day’s consensus open-model story: multiple practitioners independently described Zhipu’s GLM-5.2 as the first open-weight model that feels plausibly frontier-adjacent in daily use. @rasbt [ https://substack.com/redirect/9ce8c580-b083-48d8-b2ea-600d53df26fe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] highlighted the architecture change: beyond MLA and DSA inherited from prior GLM/DeepSeek-style designs, GLM-5.2 adds IndexShare, reusing sparse-attention top-k indices across groups of layers to reduce the cost of 1M-token inference. Community sentiment was unusually strong: @jeremyphoward [ https://substack.com/redirect/b1376fc8-b8af-4dc9-b387-a800fcdf7e8b?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] called it “at least as good as Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5” for his use, while noting its major gap is lack of vision support; @matvelloso [ https://substack.com/redirect/147f48ac-9b9a-4b06-9ee7-4529d7b3e583?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] said it was the first open model that cleared his “daily driver” bar; @ArtificialAnlys [ https://substack.com/redirect/b445bee3-155f-4c3c-a130-daede417a18d?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] placed it between GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8 on a new agentic knowledge-work eval. Zhipu also pushed availability aggressively: free via Hugging Face Inference Providers for a limited window [ https://substack.com/redirect/b9b4228a-164f-447b-8aef-ce2e395d8062?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], local GGUF support via llama.cpp/Unsloth [ https://substack.com/redirect/f7f2d15d-d2a8-49ed-9fd7-8eb3f1845518?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ], and strong app-dev deltas from 21/70 to 48/70 internal tasks vs GLM-5.1 per @ZixuanLi_ [ https://substack.com/redirect/e88280b7-b7b3-47d0-b11b-0486734841b5?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ].
Other open model releases also mattered: @poolsideai [ https://substack.com/redirect/8b0c859e-8246-4029-8fba-2d50fd2f0ffe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] released Laguna M.1 weights under Apache 2.0 with 256K context; @vllm_project [ https://substack.com/redirect/b02d457a-0870-40a5-9dc8-f6e4c5fb3307?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] described it as a 70-layer sparse MoE, 225B total / 23B active, 256 experts, top-k=16, optimized for long-horizon agentic coding with interleaved reasoning/tool use. Poolside later showed a 3-bit MLX build on Apple Silicon at ~26 tok/s and ~100 GB peak memory on an M3 Max 128 GB machine @poolsideai [ https://substack.com/redirect/8e9e4b89-c968-461c-afe6-f0c329913308?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]. On the smaller end, @cohere [ https://substack.com/redirect/9598345c-2bd2-49d0-9d7d-3120d6b9e3b8?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] pushed North Mini Code accessibility with 4-bit quantization, Ollama support, and free OpenRouter access; @ollama [ https://substack.com/redirect/b51d780e-004b-40d3-8a72-2d295d1cbfec?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] amplified support for open local deployment.
Agent Harnesses, Workflow Automation, and Coding Tooling
The center of gravity keeps moving from “model” to “model + harness + memory + SCM”: @_xjdr [ https://substack.com/redirect/287bef6d-14d5-41ed-9464-b904cd80dbb6?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] published a detailed argument that traditional git/GitHub workflows break under dozens to hundreds of concurrently running code agents: stale worktrees, diverged review state, environment setup overhead, and poor state synchronization. His proposed replacement stack combines virtual shallow checkouts, jj, Sapling-like commit stacks, cloud sync, file-level ACLs, and vertical integration from model to SCM to remote runtimes, now productized via Noumena Code / ncode with later free access to its inference engine and model @_xjdr [ https://substack.com/redirect/64fbf25a-1676-4e86-b932-3053fe69a0f9?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ]. In the same vein, @gneubig [ https://substack.com/redirect/fd352578-5c37-4f00-b795-cda54550af0a?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] argued benchmarks should evaluate the harness + LLM pair, not either in isolation; his OpenHands comparison found different winners depending on model family and cost profile.
Automation primitives are getting more teachable and reusable: @OpenAIDevs [ https://substack.com/redirect/91b74848-0cbf-4ad2-a65d-927a232978db?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] introduced Codex Record & Replay, letting users demonstrate a workflow once and turn it into an inspectable skill; @cursor_ai [ https://substack.com/redirect/1c68323a-7792-49a4-91a6-317d2bce244a?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] launched /automate, where Cursor configures triggers/instructions/tools from a natural-language task, adding Slack emoji triggers, GitHub triggers, and computer-use for cloud agents. @ClaudeDevs [ https://substack.com/redirect/caa24684-efbe-4f7b-9640-f4e9df657813?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] shipped Artifacts in Claude Code, enabling agents to turn ongoing work into shareable live pages; @_catwu [ https://substack.com/redirect/79bbf38c-c52e-4b90-8e03-42b9dae06abe?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] said this has already changed internal workflows for architecture changes and prototype sharing.
Security and review are becoming first-class agent tasks: @cognition [ https://substack.com/redirect/a3297878-b38d-4635-b7ce-4e8bf7936769?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] added automatic security review to Devin Review, and @shayanshafii [ https://substack.com/redirect/a609d5ba-076a-42cf-bfbb-d1954a494f29?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] framed Devin for Security as addressing the longstanding “finding vs fixing” split in AppSec by using agentic reasoning plus harnessing to chain lower-severity findings into confirmed severe exploits.
Top tweet in tooling by engagement: @OpenAIDevs’ Codex Record & Replay [ https://substack.com/redirect/91b74848-0cbf-4ad2-a65d-927a232978db?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] was the most engaged high-signal developer-tool post in the set, reflecting strong appetite for teach-by-demonstration agent workflows.
Benchmarks, Evaluations, and Long-Horizon Agent Measurement
Artificial Analysis launched a more realistic agentic knowledge-work benchmark: @ArtificialAnlys [ https://substack.com/redirect/d85a1a07-ec5c-45c0-8700-331296dc21c5?j=eyJ1IjoiN295MGZlIn0.SkB_ruL8LmTwq3qKVr2XDNA3a-UCPsjnydLZrCs91i8 ] introduced AA-Briefcase, built around multi-week projects, thousands of fragmented inputs, Slack/email/document corpora, and deliverables like financial models and board decks. On this benchmark, Claude Fable 5 led at 1587 Elo, with Opus 4.8 next at 1356, and GLM-5.2 at 1266 as the strongest non-Anthropic open-ish entrant mentioned. Importantly, the benchmark exposes both quality and economics:

Update from Friday, June 19, 2026


OPENAI SNAGS NOAM SHAZEER AND BUILDS A MASSIVE PARTNER NETWORK

• Noam Shazeer leaves Google for OpenAI, bringing valuable experience

• OpenAI plans to train 300,000 consultants for its new Partner Network by 2026

• Midjourney revolutionizes medical imaging with an innovative body scanner

----------------------------------------


GEMINI CO-LEAD LEAVES GOOGLE FOR OPENAI https://9to5google.com/2026/06/17/geminis-co-lead-is-leaving-google-to-join-openai/

Noam Shazeer, VP of Engineering at Google https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/google?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 and one of the two minds behind Gemini, announced on X https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/x?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 on June 18, 2026, that he is leaving the company to join OpenAI https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/OpenAI?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94. He did not specify his new role, but the move is significant: Shazeer co-led Gemini and has been in Google's AI engine room as VP of Engineering since August 2024. His resume is that of one of the most important figures in the field: a software engineer at Google from 2000 to 2021, then CEO of Character.ai, returning in August 2024 through a licensing deal between Google and Character.ai. Google's response was brief, stating they were “grateful for Noam's significant contributions over the years.” With this, the Gemini team loses one of its two captains to a direct competitor in the middle of a critical phase.

https://podcasts.apple.com/de/podcast/synthszr/id1879733990 https://open.spotify.com/show/0FJkPjKXvobgqI8U881yiF?si=wMJJ-CQxQdyuW18VXQZQOQ

Synthszr Take: Shazeer isn't just anyone; he is a co-inventor of the Transformer architecture, the 'T' in GPT. The fact that this particular person is moving from Google https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/google?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 to OpenAI https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/OpenAI?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 has an almost poetic quality: the blueprint that Google published in 2017 and then left behind is now arriving at its competitor via its own architect. In April, we wrote that OpenAI wanted to become the new Apple https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/apple?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94, and for that, it needs not just data centers but the few dozen minds who know how to build the next generation. The real moat in this industry is neither patents nor GPUs, but a handful of people you can't simply order more of. Google paid a high price to bring Shazeer back in 2024 and lost him again 22 months later—that's an expensive revolving door. Anyone who wants to stay ahead in the AI race should invest less in marketing budgets and more in understanding why the best people stay or leave.

OPENAI IS BUILDING A CONSULTING ARMY OF 300,000 https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-partner-network/

OpenAI https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/OpenAI?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 is launching the Partner Network, a global program for system integrators, strategy consultancies, and tech and data firms to build, sell, and deploy solutions around its models. $150 million is being invested in the ecosystem, and by the end of 2026, OpenAI aims to train 300,000 certified consultants. The program has three tiers (Select, Advanced, Elite) with high hurdles for sales performance, technical expertise, and deployment experience. There are also specializations in Codex https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/codex?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94, Cybersecurity, and Agents, as well as a pilot called Forward Deployed Experts, which connects partners directly to OpenAI's own Forward-Deployed-Engineering teams. OpenAI's reasoning: the company's bottleneck is no longer the models, but identifying the right use cases, redesigning workflows, and change management. No single company can deliver every solution in every market, hence the ecosystem approach.

Synthszr Take: OpenAI https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/OpenAI?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 has understood that the margin isn't in the model, but in the last mile to the customer. This is the exact same play we described in early May when OpenAI followed the Palantir https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/palantir?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 pattern with Forward Deployed Capital. Now comes the industrialized version: 300,000 certified consultants form a sales machine that turns Accenture https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/accenture?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94, Deloitte, and McKinsey into resellers without OpenAI having to pay for the consulting hours itself. This is the real moat, not GPT-5.3-Codex https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/codex?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94, because models are commoditized on a quarterly basis, while customer relationships and trained practitioners are not. Any German consulting or digital agency wondering if the effort for an Elite certification is worth it should realize that the lock-in works both ways: OpenAI locks in the consultants, and the consultants lock their clients into OpenAI. The more interesting question is what Anthropic https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/Anthropic?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 and Google https://www.synthszr.com/en/companies/google?sid=f351fd30-5cc2-4ce0-8a74-9e04c82e8e94 will do now, as a once-established partner ecosystem cannot be copied overnight. Whoever occupies the implementation playing field early wins the enterprise budgets for the next five years.

Midjourney, the company you know for turning text into images, just announced Midjourney Medical , a full-body scanner. Nobody saw this coming.Here is what it actually is. ripples that bounce back.The scanner produces a 3D map of your body down to a fraction of a millimeter, resembling an MRI but nearly 100 times faster, with Midjourney building spas in San Francisco to house the machines next year. 🤝 Google Gemini co-lead leaves for OpenAI LINKNoam Shazeer, who served as co-lead of Google's Gemini and is regarded as one of AI's top researchers, is leaving the
